board.shape: final night, own seam, unwatched, one opponent
board.question: FINAL NIGHT. Own pure at (31,18) with mass at (31,17) and (32,17). Two harvesters, one probe. The seam is UNWATCHED — no rival probe reaches it. Last night it lost a race on the RIVAL's seam. Does it convert the night, or does it carry yesterday's fear onto a board where nobody can see it?
board.canonical: Smash the pure, then strip the ring with the SECOND unit. Denial is the reason, not danger: it is the last night and the redsign is public, so they will blind-grab our seam if we leave the mass standing. Drop ON (31,18), lift hour two. Second unit opens on the MASS at (31,17), steps (32,17), lifts — because the pure is already banked, a jam on this wave costs only ring mass. The probe goes to denial; final-night probes have no frontier value. This beats taking the pure alone by about 591 of swing, not of points: the same money either way, but the ring is 591 the rival cannot have.
board.baseline: V12 banked ~1321 and left ~706 by taking the pure alone on an unwatched seam, justifying the short night by citing contest on a seam nobody could see.

rung.summary: one opponent holding chaff and an EMP, and able to buy more
rung.teaches: that a plan can be cancelled. Chaff is the only thing that denies an hour-one landing, so with chaff in play a second pass at the pure finally insures against something — and a chain that lifts late can be cut before it lifts at all. Value-first ordering stops being a nicety.

loadout.note: no ordnance — the baseline every rung assumes

checks.name: pure_first
checks.detail: harvester_p1_2 reached the pure at step 1 instead of landing on it. Every step before it is an hour a rival can take the cell first, or chaff can cut the chain short of it

checks.name: no_wake_reentry
checks.detail: a later unit walked cells an earlier one already stripped: (31,18) after harvester_p1. Those are synthetic green by the time it arrives — route the second unit outward instead

checks.name: no_repeat_pure
checks.detail: two waves went through (31,18). The first stripped it, so the second lands on synthetic green. A repeat only insures against chaff, and there is none in play here
